evals.prompt: I have local Markdown notes and saved web articles on Linux. I want to find relevant material even when I do not remember the wording. I would rather adopt an existing local-first tool than build a search system. Research the approaches worth considering, including alternatives I may not know to ask for. Do not install anything. Give me a concise recommendation with sources.
evals.expected_output: A source-grounded map of distinct approaches, at least one useful source-derived discovery, and a recommendation that respects local-first adoption rather than inventing infrastructure.
expectations: Compares substantively different retrieval approaches and ties the recommendation to local-first use on Linux rather than proposing a new search engine.
At least one follow-up read or search originates in material actually encountered, yields a relevant alternative or distinction, and is traceable in the execution evidence.
Consequential tool capabilities and limitations in the recommendation are supported by sources actually read, with uncertainty where verification is missing.
Explains significant gaps or why further exploration stopped without claiming exhaustive coverage from the call limit.

evals.prompt: What do people who actually use nvk/llm-wiki say about it? I am interested in adoption, complaints, and ongoing experience before trying it. Separate this exact implementation from the general LLM-wiki idea and other projects with similar names. Give a concise assessment with links; do not install anything.
evals.expected_output: An adoption assessment grounded in actual discussions or issue reports, distinguishing firsthand use, promotion, design concerns, confirmed fixes, and missing evidence.
expectations: Findings attributed to nvk/llm-wiki actually concern that repository; experiences with the general pattern or other implementations are kept separate.
Reads at least one firsthand user discussion or issue report and preserves what the user actually experienced rather than treating promotion as adoption.
Distinguishes reported problems, design risks, and confirmed resolutions; does not infer prevalence from stars, votes, or a selected complaint sample.
Reports sparse or inaccessible evidence as a coverage limitation rather than proof of absent adoption or community activity.

evals.prompt: Which GNU tar option lists the contents of an archive without extracting it? Give the command for backup.tar and a link to the official documentation. Keep it short.
evals.expected_output: A direct official-source lookup with the correct list command, no exploratory research loop, and no execution against an archive.
expectations: Gives tar -tf backup.tar or an equivalent GNU tar list command without extraction.
Supports the answer with official GNU tar documentation actually read.
Answers directly without unrelated alternative research, a domain map, file mutations, or executing tar against an archive.

evals.prompt: I want to keep files between a Linux laptop and an Android phone without a commercial cloud. I am not sure whether sync is even the right framing. Explore existing options starting from a relevant curated or awesome list, then read what users actually do. Explain which approaches you discovered and how the research changed the question. Do not install anything.
evals.expected_output: A traceable discovery loop from a curated category through a project and practitioner discussion to a new lead that is followed and changes the map of approaches, without inventing novelty.
expectations: Actually browses a relevant curated list or index and uses its categories or entries to choose an investigation path, rather than merely citing the index.
Reads a practitioner discussion and follows a concrete new lead from it into another source or query; the source, lead, follow-up, and finding are traceable.
Revises the framing or map of approaches from those discoveries while retaining the Linux/Android and no-commercial-cloud goal.
Keeps leads distinct from verified capabilities and first-hand experience distinct from general adoption claims, with evidence for the final practical distinctions.
